# 2. Bolt.new (StackBlitz)

**First-run shape — single prompt box, no design step**
Documented flow: type idea in the chatbox → click **Build now** → authenticate ("Google, GitHub, or email: no credit card required") → **a survey step after sign-in** → "Wait approximately five minutes while Bolt creates your app." ([quickstart](https://support.bolt.new/get-started/quickstart)) Intro doc confirms no wizard: "Type your idea into the chat, click **Build now**." ([intro-bolt](https://support.bolt.new/get-started/intro-bolt))
- Survey contents/length: **UNVERIFIED**.

**Style/colour up front:** **No** design-direction picker, chips, or theme selector at first run — nothing of the sort appears in quickstart or intro docs. Style comes only from prompt text, attached images, or a design system. ([quickstart](https://support.bolt.new/get-started/quickstart))
- Design systems exist but are heavyweight and gated: you "point Bolt to your design documentation and component library," sources being files (PDFs/images, up to 10 items or a .zip), public websites, GitHub repos, Storybook instances, or npm packages; Bolt generates a Storybook inside Bolt. **Paid Team plans only**, and takes **45–60 minutes** to set up. No logo/colour/font form. ([add-design-system](https://support.bolt.new/building/design-system/add-design-system))

**Logo upload:** Yes. Plus icon → "Attach file", or drag into chat, or drag into the **Public folder in Code view**. Accepts `.jpg .png .gif .webp .svg` plus PDFs, docs, CSV, code, config. **10 MB free / 100 MB Pro.** Behaviour: chat-attached images are used "as visual references for styling or be incorporated as project assets" depending on your instructions; if an attached image doesn't show in preview, docs advise adding it "directly to your project in Code view instead." Files added via Code view are stored in project files **without consuming tokens**. ([upload-files](https://support.bolt.new/building/upload-files))

**Reference URL / site import:** No documented "give me a URL to copy" feature. Documented start paths are: blank prompt, **Figma frame**, Google Stitch, marketplace templates, team templates, existing repository ("from GitHub or Lovable"), and uploaded files. ([start-project](https://support.bolt.new/building/start-project)) Figma import: plus icon → "Import Figma frame" → paste frame URL (requires being logged into Figma); or prefix a Figma URL with `bolt.new`. ([figma integration](https://support.bolt.new/integrations/figma), [bolt blog](https://bolt.new/blog/import-figma-frames-into-existing-bolt-projects))
- Public **websites** are accepted only as a *design-system source*, not as a project-creation path. ([add-design-system](https://support.bolt.new/building/design-system/add-design-system))
- Importing the user's own live site (content migration): **UNVERIFIED / not documented.**

**Prompt enhance: YES — and it's a questionnaire, which is notable.** Plus icon (bottom-left of chatbox) → **"Enhance prompt"** → a dialog titled "Help us enhance your prompt" where you "answer each question to give Bolt more information about what you're building"; Bolt then "generates a recommended prompt, which you can edit." ([interacting-ai](https://support.bolt.new/building/using-bolt/interacting-ai))
- The exact questions asked: **UNVERIFIED** — docs describe the mechanism, not the question list.

**Plan mode:** "a chat mode where you can plan and ask questions without making changes to your code," and you can "begin your Bolt project in Plan Mode right from the first prompt" on the homepage. Whether Plan mode itself is billed differently: **UNVERIFIED** (docs only say planning first saves tokens). ([plan-mode](https://support.bolt.new/best-practices/plan-mode))

**Cost:** Free = **1M tokens/month** with a **300K tokens/day** cap; free tokens don't roll over ("fixed one-month buckets"). Paid tokens roll over two months. "Most of your token usage comes from Bolt reading, understanding, and syncing your project files." ([tokens](https://support.bolt.new/account-and-subscription/tokens)) Concrete first-build datapoint: the quickstart's "Pet Name Picker" consumed **~204K of the 300K daily free tokens** — i.e. one toy app is ~two-thirds of a free day. ([quickstart](https://support.bolt.new/get-started/quickstart))

([screenshots](https://v0.app/docs/screenshots))

# 4. Base44 (Wix-owned)

**First-run shape — richest entry surface of the four; 2–3 steps**
The first prompt screen is a freeform box **plus a mode dropdown and multiple entry paths**: plain-language prompt; **Plan mode**; **Start from URL**; **Import from Figma**; file attachments; tool connectors; and speech-to-text. ([starting-from-your-first-prompt](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/starting-from-your-first-prompt))
- Default path: enter prompt (optionally with mode/attachments/connectors) → sign up (free, no credit card) → watch it build in a live preview. ([Quick-start-guide](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/Quick-start-guide))
- **Plan mode adds a Q&A step:** it "turns a short conversation into a structured plan you can adjust before Base44 builds anything" — you answer the AI's questions, review/edit the structured plan, then click **"Start building."** So 3 steps, and it lets you "think through your idea without needing to know what to specify in advance" before committing credits. ([starting-from-your-first-prompt](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/starting-from-your-first-prompt))

**Style/colour up front:** No chips/theme picker in the prompt box; by default the AI "automatically designs your app's appearance, choosing colors, arranging buttons, and organizing menus." ([Quick-start-guide](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/Quick-start-guide))
- **However** — the workspace **Design system / brand kit** is the strongest up-front branding mechanism of any of the four: define "your brand's colors, fonts, logo, and components once, then apply one consistent look across your apps," including corner radius, shadow depth, spacing. Sources can be a brand description, Figma import, **website URL**, npm package, or custom design files. Crucially: "your default design system is preselected, so the app is built to match your brand **from the first prompt**." Requires **Builder plan or higher**, web apps only, and **costs no credits**. ([Design-system](https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/Design-system))
- Post-generation: a **Theme panel** (palette icon) where you "Click any color role to update it across your entire app," plus Edit mode for direct element manipulation. ([Design](https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/Design))

**Logo upload:** Yes, explicitly. App dashboard → **Overview** → click the **Edit** icon on the logo → upload your own image file **or generate one with AI**. Other images upload from the AI chat, your computer, or Google Drive, or at runtime via the UploadFile integration; everything lands in the app's **file library** ("automatically stored in the file library"). ([Using-media](https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/Using-media))
- Hosting mechanics (URL structure, CDN): **UNVERIFIED** — docs don't state them.

**Reference URL — the most explicit of the four.** "Start from URL" offers **two options**:
1. **Content & Design** — "Recreates the site's content and layout to build a similar site."
2. **Design only** — "Uses the site's visual style to create a new site with the same look and feel."

It recreates the visible frontend: page structure, key content sections, visual hierarchy, and familiar UI patterns (hero sections, cards, lists). Available on all plans **including Free**; **consumes credits**; you must own the site or hold full rights to its content, design and images; it does **not** copy private backend code, hidden data, or third-party integrations. ([starting-from-your-first-prompt](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/starting-from-your-first-prompt))
- Base44's own docs describe it as capturing "the look and feel of any public webpage, with no credentials needed" — i.e. frontend capture, no login. Whether the pipeline is a screenshot, a DOM scrape, or both: **UNVERIFIED** (docs describe outcome, not method). ([migrating-an-existing-app](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/migrating-an-existing-app))

**Own-site content migration — the only one of the four with a real migration product.** Distinct from Start from URL: "Migrate from another platform" **"connects to your actual account and brings over your real data, schema, and frontend code"** via OAuth, API tokens, or database access. Preserves field types, relationships, primary/foreign keys. "Base44 imports 100 items from each entity first so you can preview your app before committing"; you choose which entities to import; large datasets take time and migration continues in the background if you leave the page. Known gap: WordPress custom fields aren't imported. ([migrating-an-existing-app](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/migrating-an-existing-app))

**First-prompt attachments:** Images and PDFs as visual references for design matching; spreadsheets/CSV read for column structure and sample data; Word/txt/Markdown inform content and structure. Upload from computer or Google Drive. Tool connectors (Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub) can be attached to the initial prompt so the first build already reads/creates events or posts updates. ([starting-from-your-first-prompt](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/starting-from-your-first-prompt))

**Prompt enhance:** **Not documented** as a button. Plan mode is the functional equivalent. **UNVERIFIED** whether an enhance control exists in the UI.

**Cost:** Free = **5 credits/day, 25/month max**. Message credits by scope: simple visual/text change ≈ **0.5**, small feature improvement ≈ **1**, complex module ≈ **2**, large-scale app change ≈ **3–4**. **Discuss mode = 0.3 credits/message.** Integration credits: 1 per email, 1 per generated image, ~1 per LLM call (automatic model), 1 per automation run. **Manual editing (dragging elements, changing text directly) costs nothing.** Design systems cost nothing. ([Credits](https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits), [AI-chat-modes](https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/AI-chat-modes), [Design-system](https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/Design-system))
- Credit cost of the initial generation specifically: **UNVERIFIED**.
- Note a doc inconsistency: the chat-modes page names the three modes **Default / Discuss / Edit**, while the getting-started page calls the planning mode **Plan mode**. ([AI-chat-modes](https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/AI-chat-modes) vs [starting-from-your-first-prompt](https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/starting-from-your-first-prompt))

# Cross-product comparison

| | Lovable | Bolt | v0 | Base44 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First-run | Prompt box + **3 design previews** | Prompt box, no design step | Prompt box, leanest | Prompt box + **mode dropdown + 4 entry paths** |
| Steps to first output | 2 (prompt → pick design) | ~3 (prompt → Build now → auth+survey) | 3 (sign in → new chat → prompt) | 2 default; 3 in Plan mode |
| Style asked up front | **Yes — pick 1 of 3 rendered previews, refine ≤6×** | No | No | No (auto), unless a default design system is set |
| Logo upload | Yes, chat/public folder/CDN >10 MB | Yes, chat or Code view Public folder | Yes, 5 MB free | **Yes — dedicated dashboard logo slot, or AI-generate** |
| Reference URL | **Yes** via `html=` API param (fetched server-side) | No (websites only as design-system source) | No — screenshot upload instead | **Yes — Content&Design or Design-only** |
| Own-site migration | Not documented | Not documented | ZIP/Git only | **Yes — real credentialed data+schema migration** |
| Prompt enhance | **Not documented** (contrary to brief) | **Yes — a question dialog**, then editable generated prompt | **Not documented** (contrary to brief) | Not documented (Plan mode instead) |
| Free tier | 5 credits/day, 30/mo | 1M tokens/mo, 300K/day | $5/mo + 7 msgs/day | 5 credits/day, 25/mo |

**Two findings that contradict the brief's assumptions:** Lovable's documented enhance-prompt feature does not exist in current docs (design guidance replaced that job), while **Bolt** is the one with a genuine enhance-prompt questionnaire. And Lovable is the only product that puts an explicit visual-direction choice *before* the first build.

# 4. Base44 (Wix-owned)

**First-run shape — richest entry surface of the four; 2–3 steps**
The first prompt screen is a freeform box **plus a mode dropdown and multiple entry paths**: plain-language prompt; **Plan mode**; **Start from URL**; **Import from Figma**; file attachments; tool connectors; and speech-to-text. 2. **Design only** — "Uses the site's visual style to create a new site with the same look and feel."

It recreates the visible frontend: page structure, key content sections, visual hierarchy, and familiar UI patterns (hero sections, cards, lists). | | Lovable | Bolt | v0 | Base44 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First-run | Prompt box + **3 design previews** | Prompt box, no design step | Prompt box, leanest | Prompt box + **mode dropdown + 4 entry paths** |
| Steps to first output | 2 (prompt → pick design) | ~3 (prompt → Build now → auth+survey) | 3 (sign in → new chat → prompt) | 2 default; 3 in Plan mode |
| Style asked up front | **Yes — pick 1 of 3 rendered previews, refine ≤6×** | No | No | No (auto), unless a default design system is set |
| Logo upload | Yes, chat/public folder/CDN >10 MB | Yes, chat or Code view Public folder | Yes, 5 MB free | **Yes — dedicated dashboard logo slot, or AI-generate** |
| Reference URL | **Yes** via `html=` API param (fetched server-side) | No (websites only as design-system source) | No — screenshot upload instead | **Yes — Content&Design or Design-only** |

## What I built

**`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`** (new) — a server component at `/dashboard/billing`, `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>`, `max-w-4xl px-6 py-10`, matching the dashboard's monochrome `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10` / `text-sm` / `tabular-nums` idiom throughout. Five sections:

1. **Spend summary** — three tiles: credits left, used in the last 30 days, and the user's own `averageBuildCredits`.
2. **Spending cap** — when set, a `role="progressbar"` bar with `aria-valuenow/min/max` and a real `aria-label`, spent-of-cap, remaining, and an amber state plus honest wording when reached; when unset, one line pointing at Settings. Reuses `getSpendCapStatus`/`spentInWindow` so the number shown is the one the cap actually enforces.
3. **Add credits** — `<TopUpButton>` fed from the server's own `CREDIT_PACKS`, or the honest unavailable message.
4. **Credit statement** — paginated table (25/page, `?page=N`, clamped), newest-first with `[{createdAt:"desc"},{id:"desc"}]` so row 0 on page 1 is the row that defines the balance. Columns: When (UTC), What for, Change (signed, coloured), Balance (`balanceAfter` — the running balance). Build charges link to `/projects/<id>`. `<caption class="sr-only">`, `scope="col"` headers, `nav aria-label` + `rel="prev"/"next"` pager, "Showing X–Y of Z".
5. **What a build costs** — `estimateCredits()`'s first caller.

**`app/dashboard/billing/ledger.ts`** (new) — `describeReason`, deterministic UTC date/time formatters, signed-credit formatting.

**`app/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx`** — added optional `enabled` (default `true`) and `packs` (default = the existing hardcoded list, so the dashboard's prop-less `<TopUpButton />` is unchanged); `focus-visible:` rings and `type="button"` on all three controls; removed a misleading `aria-expanded={false}` on a trigger that unmounts when opened.

## How each `reason` is decoded

| Stored | Shown |
|---|---|
| `build` | "Site build" + link to the project; if `buildId` went NULL (project deleted), "The site this was for has since been deleted." |
| `signup_grant` | "Welcome credits" / "Added free when you created your account" |
| `stripe:<session>` | "Credit purchase" / "Paid top-up" — session id dropped |
| `reward:<platform>:<hash>` | "Discord/Instagram/… reward" via `PLATFORM_LABELS` |
| `reward:<platform>:pending:<hash>` | "… reward — on hold" / "Recorded. The credits are added once the hold period is up." (the delta-0 row) |
| anything else | "Credits added" / "Credits used" / "Account note" by sign |

No raw hash, session id, or raw `reason` reaches the customer — including via `title`, which the admin page uses but this one deliberately omits. The unknown branch describes by direction of money rather than echoing the string.

## What I verified about charging (`app/api/generate/route.ts`)

- `chargeForBuild` is called **only** inside the `succeeded = true` branch. Every failure path (thrown error, abort, no output) writes `creditsCharged: 0` and touches no ledger row.
- `totals` accumulate across **both** attempts of the repair loop, then a single `costMicros`/`creditsFor`/`chargeForBuild` runs after the loop — so a run that fails, self-repairs, then succeeds is charged **once for the whole run including the repair**. The page says exactly that.
- A zero-cost success writes no ledger row at all. Hence the statement's footnote: a build reaches it only if it succeeded *and* had measured cost.
- "Credits don't expire" checked against `lib/retention.ts` — `CreditLedger` is in `NEVER_PRUNED` ("Retained permanently") and no expiry logic exists anywhere.

## With Stripe unconfigured

The page renders in full — tiles, cap, statement, cost info. The Add credits section renders `<TopUpButton enabled={false} />`, which returns plain text ("Top-ups aren't available right now — card payments aren't set up on this deployment. Your credits and everything on this page are unaffected."), never a button that would 503 against `/api/billing/checkout`.

## Claims I chose not to make

- **File storage:** yes, first-party — "a first-party file library integrated directly into each app," per-app (not shared across apps in a workspace), "no hard storage limit per app," per-file caps (images up to 40MB while building, video 100MB, documents 5–15MB by format). https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/Using-media.md

- **Payments:** Base44 Payments (Wix) or Stripe. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/setting-up-wix-payments.md
- Caveat on the marketing: Base44 still ships a large connector catalog (Slack, GitHub, Snowflake, Databricks, Zapier, Airtable, LinkedIn, Google Search Console…), so "no integrations needed" means *no third-party account required for the core stack*, not that integrations don't exist. https://docs.base44.com/llms.txt
- Security posture claims: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR + DPA on request, PCI DSS payment processing, pen testing, bug bounty; data residency (EU/UK/US) on Elite and Enterprise. Cloud provider is **not disclosed** in the docs. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/security-overview.md

**Templates / starters**
- There is a template marketplace — "your shortcut to building great apps on Base44," community-created, free or paid with creators setting prices and **no commission taken by Base44**; plus private workspace templates. Time framing only ("launch your next project in minutes"); **no quantified credit- or cost-saving claim in the docs**. https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/App-templates · https://base44.com/templates
- Template count: search results describe "100+ ready-made app templates"; the official docs page gives no number — treat "100+" as **unverified**.

**Pricing (official page, fetched 2026-08-22; figures are monthly-equivalent billed annually, 20% annual discount)**
- Free: $0 — 25 message credits/mo, 100 integration credits/mo, up to 5 apps, includes auth, database, analytics
- Starter: $16/mo — 100 message credits, 2,000 integration credits, unlimited apps, in-app code edits, domain connection
- Builder: $40/mo — 250 message credits, 10,000 integration credits, + AI model selection, free domain 1 yr, GitHub integration

- Source: https://base44.com/pricing
- **Unverified:** the month-to-month (non-annual) sticker prices; the page presents annual-equivalent numbers only.

**Credit mechanics (official)**
- Two meters. **Message credits** = prompting the AI to build/debug/rewrite. **Integration credits** = your live app using Base44's built-in services. External APIs with your own keys don't consume them. https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits.md
- Cost is variable, not per-action: "Credits are based on how much work the system has to do, not on how small the change looks" — small tweaks ~0.5 credits, app-wide changes 3–4.
- Published integration-credit rates: email 1 · email from custom domain 2 · push notification 1 · file upload/extraction 1 each · image generation 1 · video generation 5 per second · speech 1 per 50 characters · LLM call ~1 (Automatic) / ~5 (Gemini 3 Flash) / ~15 (GPT-5.4) · automation run 1 plus whatever it calls.
- **No rollover** — unused monthly credits expire at cycle end; free-plan daily credits reset at midnight local (or UTC). When integration credits run out, actions fail with an error and you get an email; end users see a generic error. Same page.
- **Unverified:** whether mid-cycle top-up credit packs exist and at what price. The billing doc does not mention them and only discusses upgrading plans. https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Billing-and-plans.md

**Security incident — the Wiz auth bypass (verified from the primary source)**
- Two **unauthenticated** API endpoints — `api/apps/{app_id}/auth/register` and `api/apps/{app_id}/auth/verify-otp` — let anyone register a verified account on any app using only the non-secret `app_id`, which is publicly visible in app URLs and `manifest.json`. This bypassed all access controls **including SSO**, even with registration disabled.
- Timeline: discovered and reported to Wix/Base44 **July 9, 2025**; fix verified by Wiz **July 10, 2025**; Wix confirmed resolution **July 13, 2025**; public disclosure **July 29, 2025**. Wix found "no evidence of past abuse" and "no indication of compromise across Base44 user-base during the vulnerable period."
- Impact framing: affected apps included internal chatbots, knowledge bases, PII/HR tools.
- Primary source: https://www.wiz.io/blog/critical-vulnerability-base44
- Press coverage: https://thehackernews.com/2025/07/wiz-uncovers-critical-access-bypass.html · https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/authentication-flaw-base44/ · https://www.securityweek.com/flaw-in-vibe-coding-platform-base44-exposed-private-enterprise-applications/ · https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/critical-flaw-vibe-coding-base44-exposed-apps
- Notable follow-on: Base44 now documents Wiz vulnerability scanning and a security-scan feature in-product. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/scanning-with-wiz.md · https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/running-a-security-scan.md

**Credit-burn commentary (secondary, flagged)**
- Aggregator blogs citing Reddit report: burning 17.5 credits in ten minutes on a 2.5-credit task due to retries; ~3.5–4 credits per prompt and $600 spent in three months; a Pro user burning 500 credits in three days with upgrade-to-Elite as the only remedy. # Cross-cutting comparison

| | v0 | Base44 | Rocket.new |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend/DB | Third-party via Vercel Marketplace (Neon/Supabase/Upstash); Vercel Blob is first-party storage | **First-party** MongoDB-compatible NoSQL + Deno serverless functions | Third-party Supabase (your own account, OAuth) |
| Auth | None built in — you wire Supabase/Clerk/NextAuth | **Built in**: email/password, Google/Microsoft/Facebook/Apple, SSO on Elite | Supabase Auth, auto-configured |
| Server-side code | Yes — Next.js RSC, API routes, server actions | Yes — Deno functions with HTTP endpoints | Frontend on Netlify; server logic in Supabase edge functions |
| Hosting | Vercel projects | Base44 (`*.base44.app`) | Netlify (Rocket's default account or yours) |
| Meter | Tokens → credits, $-denominated | Message credits + integration credits | Single credit balance |
| Free tier | $5 credits/mo, 7 msgs/day | 25 msg + 100 integration credits/mo, 5 apps | 20 credits, one-time |
| Known incident | Credit-burn complaints on Vercel's own forum | Wiz auth bypass, disclosed Jul 29 2025, patched in ~24h | None found |

The sharpest verified contrast for your purposes: **Base44 is the only one of the three that owns its database, auth, file storage, email and analytics end to end** — and that same first-party auth layer is exactly what failed in the July 2025 Wiz disclosure. v0 and Rocket both delegate the backend to third parties (Vercel Marketplace partners; Supabase), which pushes the account sprawl, and the security surface, onto the user.

**Explicitly unverified items:** v0's token-metering switch date; v0 month-to-month legacy Premium availability; Base44's monthly (non-annual) prices, mid-cycle credit top-ups, cloud provider, template count, and the $80M Wix acquisition figure; Rocket's add-on credit pricing, per-message credit rate, Trustpilot score/count, and whether Next.js server routes are deployed as Netlify functions.</result>

# 2. Base44 (acquired by Wix)

**Backend / database — genuinely first-party**
- Base44 runs its own backend-as-a-service: "a complete backend-as-a-service (BaaS)" that is "the same backend that powers Base44's app editor." https://docs.base44.com/developers/backend/overview/backend-service-basics.md
- Database is **first-party NoSQL, MongoDB-compatible**: "Each entity is a schema that defines the structure for documents in a collection, stored in Base44's NoSQL database" and "The database is MongoDB-compatible, so you can use MongoDB operators when querying through the SDK." Entities are JSON Schema files; row-level and field-level security rules. https://docs.base44.com/developers/backend/resources/entities/overview.md
- Custom server logic: "Backend functions run on Deno" — Deno-powered serverless functions, each with its own HTTP endpoint at `https://<your-app-domain>/functions/<function-name>`, 5-minute max execution. https://docs.base44.com/developers/backend/resources/backend-functions/overview.md

**Auth — built in, no third-party account needed**
- All new apps ship with custom login pages; Base44 "handles authentication securely behind the scenes" with login, registration, password recovery and reset. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/Managing-login-and-registration.md
- Methods: email/password; social providers **Google, Microsoft, Facebook, Apple**; custom Google OAuth with your own GCP credentials; OIDC external providers; **SSO (Okta etc.) is Elite-plan only**. Visibility modes: public (no login) / public (login required) / private (invite or SSO only). Same page.

**Architecture and hosting**
- Apps are hosted by Base44 itself, no deploy step: "Built-in hosting — when your app is ready, it's instantly live and shareable… No deployment process, no setup." https://base44.com/
- Every app gets a free `myapp.base44.app` URL; custom domains via CNAME, SSL issued and renewed automatically, up to 150 domains/subdomains per app; domains purchasable through Base44 (GoDaddy or Wix registrar). https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/Setting-up-your-custom-domain.md
- So: frontend + a real hosted backend (Base44 API, entities, Deno functions). Not client-only.

**Verifying the "all-in-one, no integrations needed" claim — what's actually included**
- Homepage claims: "Ship something real with vibe coding — without touching a server, wiring up a payment provider, or configuring a database"; "The whole stack. No setup slowdown."; "Backend and storage, built in"; "One-click integrations"; "Get paid directly through Base44." https://base44.com/
- **Database:** yes, first-party (above).
- **Auth:** yes, first-party (above).
- **File storage:** yes, first-party — "a first-party file library integrated directly into each app," per-app (not shared across apps in a workspace), "no hard storage limit per app," per-file caps (images up to 40MB while building, video 100MB, documents 5–15MB by format). https://docs.base44.com/Building-your-app/Using-media.md
- **Email:** built-in sending exists and is metered in integration credits (1 credit/email, 2 for custom-domain sending) — plus optional Gmail and Resend connectors. https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits.md · https://docs.base44.com/Integrations/Resend-integration.md · https://docs.base44.com/Integrations/gmail-connector.md
- **Analytics:** built in — App Analytics (traffic, sales, customizable dashboard), Session Recordings, App Logs Explorer, plus an SDK analytics module. https://docs.base44.com/documentation/performance-and-seo/app-analytics.md · https://docs.base44.com/documentation/performance-and-seo/session-recordings.md
- **Payments:** Base44 Payments (Wix) or Stripe. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/setting-up-wix-payments.md
- Caveat on the marketing: Base44 still ships a large connector catalog (Slack, GitHub, Snowflake, Databricks, Zapier, Airtable, LinkedIn, Google Search Console…), so "no integrations needed" means *no third-party account required for the core stack*, not that integrations don't exist. https://docs.base44.com/llms.txt
- Security posture claims: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR + DPA on request, PCI DSS payment processing, pen testing, bug bounty; data residency (EU/UK/US) on Elite and Enterprise. Cloud provider is **not disclosed** in the docs. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/security-overview.md

**Templates / starters**
- There is a template marketplace — "your shortcut to building great apps on Base44," community-created, free or paid with creators setting prices and **no commission taken by Base44**; plus private workspace templates. Time framing only ("launch your next project in minutes"); **no quantified credit- or cost-saving claim in the docs**. https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/App-templates · https://base44.com/templates
- Template count: search results describe "100+ ready-made app templates"; the official docs page gives no number — treat "100+" as **unverified**.

**Pricing (official page, fetched 2026-08-22; figures are monthly-equivalent billed annually, 20% annual discount)**
- Free: $0 — 25 message credits/mo, 100 integration credits/mo, up to 5 apps, includes auth, database, analytics
- Starter: $16/mo — 100 message credits, 2,000 integration credits, unlimited apps, in-app code edits, domain connection
- Builder: $40/mo — 250 message credits, 10,000 integration credits, + AI model selection, free domain 1 yr, GitHub integration
- Pro: $80/mo — 500 message credits, 20,000 integration credits, + early beta access
- Elite: $160/mo — 1,200 message credits, 50,000 integration credits, + premium support (and SSO, per the auth doc)
- Source: https://base44.com/pricing
- **Unverified:** the month-to-month (non-annual) sticker prices; the page presents annual-equivalent numbers only.

**Credit mechanics (official)**
- Two meters. **Message credits** = prompting the AI to build/debug/rewrite. **Integration credits** = your live app using Base44's built-in services. External APIs with your own keys don't consume them. https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Credits.md
- Cost is variable, not per-action: "Credits are based on how much work the system has to do, not on how small the change looks" — small tweaks ~0.5 credits, app-wide changes 3–4.
- Published integration-credit rates: email 1 · email from custom domain 2 · push notification 1 · file upload/extraction 1 each · image generation 1 · video generation 5 per second · speech 1 per 50 characters · LLM call ~1 (Automatic) / ~5 (Gemini 3 Flash) / ~15 (GPT-5.4) · automation run 1 plus whatever it calls.

- **Unverified:** whether mid-cycle top-up credit packs exist and at what price. The billing doc does not mention them and only discusses upgrading plans. https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Billing-and-plans.md

**Security incident — the Wiz auth bypass (verified from the primary source)**
- Two **unauthenticated** API endpoints — `api/apps/{app_id}/auth/register` and `api/apps/{app_id}/auth/verify-otp` — let anyone register a verified account on any app using only the non-secret `app_id`, which is publicly visible in app URLs and `manifest.json`. This bypassed all access controls **including SSO**, even with registration disabled.
- Timeline: discovered and reported to Wix/Base44 **July 9, 2025**; fix verified by Wiz **July 10, 2025**; Wix confirmed resolution **July 13, 2025**; public disclosure **July 29, 2025**. Wix found "no evidence of past abuse" and "no indication of compromise across Base44 user-base during the vulnerable period."
- Impact framing: affected apps included internal chatbots, knowledge bases, PII/HR tools.
- Primary source: https://www.wiz.io/blog/critical-vulnerability-base44
- Press coverage: https://thehackernews.com/2025/07/wiz-uncovers-critical-access-bypass.html · https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/authentication-flaw-base44/ · https://www.securityweek.com/flaw-in-vibe-coding-platform-base44-exposed-private-enterprise-applications/ · https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/critical-flaw-vibe-coding-base44-exposed-apps
- Notable follow-on: Base44 now documents Wiz vulnerability scanning and a security-scan feature in-product. https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/scanning-with-wiz.md · https://docs.base44.com/Setting-up-your-app/running-a-security-scan.md

**Credit-burn commentary (secondary, flagged)**
- Aggregator blogs citing Reddit report: burning 17.5 credits in ten minutes on a 2.5-credit task due to retries; ~3.5–4 credits per prompt and $600 spent in three months; a Pro user burning 500 credits in three days with upgrade-to-Elite as the only remedy. # Cross-cutting comparison

| | v0 | Base44 | Rocket.new |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend/DB | Third-party via Vercel Marketplace (Neon/Supabase/Upstash); Vercel Blob is first-party storage | **First-party** MongoDB-compatible NoSQL + Deno serverless functions | Third-party Supabase (your own account, OAuth) |
| Auth | None built in — you wire Supabase/Clerk/NextAuth | **Built in**: email/password, Google/Microsoft/Facebook/Apple, SSO on Elite | Supabase Auth, auto-configured |
| Server-side code | Yes — Next.js RSC, API routes, server actions | Yes — Deno functions with HTTP endpoints | Frontend on Netlify; server logic in Supabase edge functions |
| Hosting | Vercel projects | Base44 (`*.base44.app`) | Netlify (Rocket's default account or yours) |
| Meter | Tokens → credits, $-denominated | Message credits + integration credits | Single credit balance |
| Free tier | $5 credits/mo, 7 msgs/day | 25 msg + 100 integration credits/mo, 5 apps | 20 credits, one-time |
| Known incident | Credit-burn complaints on Vercel's own forum | Wiz auth bypass, disclosed Jul 29 2025, patched in ~24h | None found |

The sharpest verified contrast for your purposes: **Base44 is the only one of the three that owns its database, auth, file storage, email and analytics end to end** — and that same first-party auth layer is exactly what failed in the July 2025 Wiz disclosure. v0 and Rocket both delegate the backend to third parties (Vercel Marketplace partners; Supabase), which pushes the account sprawl, and the security surface, onto the user.

**Explicitly unverified items:** v0's token-metering switch date; v0 month-to-month legacy Premium availability; Base44's monthly (non-annual) prices, mid-cycle credit top-ups, cloud provider, template count, and the $80M Wix acquisition figure; Rocket's add-on credit pricing, per-message credit rate, Trustpilot score/count, and whether Next.js server routes are deployed as Netlify functions.</result>

## 2. Durable (durable.co → durable.com)

Note: durable.co now 301-redirects to **durable.com**, and the help center is **help.durable.com**. Durable relaunched as "the complete AI business builder" in a **17 March 2026** blog post.

Durable's own product page says only: **"Answer 3 questions about your business."**
Source: https://durable.com/ai-website-builder

The three fields, in order (consistent across two independent hands-on reviews):
1. **"What type of business are you building?"** — pick from preset categories; free-text description also accepted (e.g. "a vegan café specialized in organic coffee")
2. **"What is the name of your business?"** — with an **optional AI business-name generator** if you don't have one

**Not asked at all.** Reviews are explicit that the AI picks it: "It will automatically select a layout, color palette, and relevant images" from business type alone. Restyling happens post-generation — Durable has a one-click **restyle** button that changes colors, fonts, text and image positions, plus premade palettes.
Sources *(review sites)*: https://www.makingthatwebsite.com/durable-ai-website-builder-review/ · https://www.websiteplanet.com/website-builders/durable/

- **Generation: yes**, but as a **separate tool after site creation**, not in the 3-question flow. Durable ships an **AI Brand Builder** and an **AI Logo Generator** that produce logo, colour palette and font scheme; the logo is output in multiple formats (social profiles, printed merch) and the brand applies across invoices, forms and social images.
Sources: https://durable.com/ai-brand-builder · https://durable.co/ai-tools/logoai · https://www.websiteplanet.com/website-builders/durable/ · https://www.fahimai.com/durable-ai-website-builder

## 3. Framer

### Big caveat on naming
Framer's AI entry point has been renamed at least twice. The original consumer-facing **"Start with AI"** (a new-project option) became **Wireframer**, and by 2026 Framer's own Academy course is titled **"Get Started with Framer Agents"** — the lesson formerly at `/academy/lessons/wireframer` now redirects into the Framer Agents course.
Sources: https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/wireframer · https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/framer-agents-generation-layout-style · https://www.framer.com/ai/

**"Workshop" is a different thing** — it is Framer's AI **component** builder (Cmd+K → "Workshop"), for logic-heavy components like calculators, forms, quizzes and countdown timers. It is *not* the site-onboarding flow. Best source is a review (oma-kase.com/blog/framer-ai-workshop-plugin); Framer's own /ai page describes it as "AI Code Components — build custom interactive features from descriptions."
Source: https://www.framer.com/ai/

### Onboarding sequence — **there is no question sequence. It's a single prompt box.**
Framer's own solutions page gives a 4-step framing:
1. **"Start from a prompt"** — "Describe the site, audience, or page you need, then let Framer AI generate a strong first direction." Entry points can be "a prompt, brief, blank canvas, or existing idea."
2. Refine the design visually on canvas (structure, copy, styling, sections, images, responsive behavior)
3. Add real site systems (CMS, SEO metadata, forms, analytics, components)
4. Publish and iterate
Source: https://www.framer.com/solutions/ai-website-builder/

Mechanically: new project → **Insert → Wireframer** (or Cmd+K), which opens a chat box. The box offers **preset templates** (e.g. "a personal page with a list of projects") or your own typed prompt. **One step to first output.**
Source *(Framer University — community/partner blog, not framer.com)*: https://framer.university/blog/the-new-ai-workflow-for-building-websites

Framer's Academy notes the prompt should be specific about subject and desired sections (navigation, feature section, testimonial, footer), and that Wireframer generates responsive sections with navigation, headings, image placeholders and AI-written body copy — **all breakpoints (desktop/tablet/mobile) generated simultaneously**.
Sources: https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/wireframer · *(review)* https://hostadvice.com/ai-app-builders/framer-review/

### Style / colour / design direction
**No separate style step and no theme cards or adjective chips.** Style is expressed inside the prompt itself — Framer's own example prompt on /ai: *"Generate a homepage for Bloom... Make it minimalistic and dark, with releases, research themes, public trust, and CTAs."* A review notes the prompt box deliberately has no "AI Styles" settings.
Sources: https://www.framer.com/ai/ · *(review)* https://hostadvice.com/ai-app-builders/framer-review/

**Post-generation** you get shuffle-style controls: shuffle fonts and colour palettes, shuffle a specific section to randomize colours within it, AI text rewrite, AI translate. Framer's own /ai page also lists an **AI Site Review** (contrast issues, typos, alt-text gaps, SEO problems, style inconsistencies).
Sources: *(tutorial site)* https://designcode.io/framer-web-design-ai/ · https://www.framer.com/ai/

### Logo
- **Upload: yes**, but as normal post-generation editing — you replace placeholder images and upload your logo on canvas. *(Framer University: framer.university/blog/the-new-ai-workflow-for-building-websites)*
- **AI logo generation: UNVERIFIED** — Framer's /ai feature list includes AI image generation for visuals but no logo generator per se.
- **Palette extraction from a logo: UNVERIFIED.**

### Reference URL — **yes, this is Framer's differentiator**
Framer's own /ai page states the agents accept **"Upload images, files, or URLs to guide AI toward the exact result"**, plus canvas context (select layers and add them as chat context) and model selection (GPT, Sonnet, Opus, or Fable). The Academy lesson adds that agents can **rebuild UI from screenshots**.
Sources: https://www.framer.com/ai/ · https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/framer-agents-generation-layout-style

**Caveat:** this is described as context for the *agent inside a project*, not as a first-screen "paste a URL to clone" field. Whether a URL can be supplied at the very first new-project prompt: **UNVERIFIED**.

### Import existing site
**UNVERIFIED / not documented.** Framer's own pages make no import claim; the URL-as-context capability above is the closest thing.

### Business-data scraping
**UNVERIFIED.** No GBP/social scraping documented.

### Time-to-first-output
Framer's own pages make **no numeric claim** — /solutions/ai-website-builder gives no time estimate. Third parties claim: "under 30 seconds" for a responsive copy-filled homepage *(hostadvice review)*, "30 seconds to one minute" for a full page layout *(designcode.io)*, and "from prompt to published site in minutes" *(Framer University)*.

## 4. Hostinger — two separate products, don't conflate them

### 4a. Hostinger AI Website Builder (the site builder)
**Onboarding fields, in order:**
1. **Brand name**
2. **Type of website** — a picker: Online store, Blog, Business, Portfolio, Landing page, Other
3. **Description** — free text, **max 700 characters including spaces**; Hostinger's guidance: "The more descriptive you are, the better results you'll get!"

Hostinger's marketing summarizes it as: you only need "a name, a website type, and a short description."
Sources: https://www.hostinger.com/blog/ai-website-builder-unique-websites · https://www.hostinger.com/ai-website-builder

**Time claim (vendor):** the AI prepares structure, layout and mobile view, generates content and picks images, and "your unique website will be ready in **less than a minute**."

**Style/colour step, logo, reference URL, import:** **UNVERIFIED** — the official support article does not document any of these at onboarding.

**Flow per Hostinger's official support article:** pricing page → hPanel → Websites → Add Website → **AI Builder** → a text field where "you can write your prompt in more than 80 languages" (or select a template) → choose a domain or use a temporary one → split-pane view (prompts left, live preview right) → refine → Publish. Then a separate choice of **Manual** editing vs **Agentic** (conversational, consumes AI credits).
Sources: https://www.hostinger.com/support/how-to-create-a-web-app-using-hostinger-horizons/ · https://www.hostinger.com/support/7266945-how-to-use-hostinger-ai-website-builder/

**Clarifying questions:** Hostinger's official prompting article confirms "some clarifying questions from Hostinger AI Builder may show clickable answer options" — i.e. **chip-style answers exist**. A **prompt-guidance planning agent** that asks targeted questions to auto-generate optimized prompts launched **January 2026**, alongside a select-and-edit visual editor and 100+ new templates. **The exact questions it asks are UNVERIFIED.**
Sources: https://www.hostinger.com/support/prompting-hostinger-horizons-build-your-web-app-effectively/ · *(review)* https://bloggingjoy.com/hosting/hostinger-horizons-review/

**Wireframes can be uploaded as prompts.** Logo upload/generation, reference URL, and site import: **UNVERIFIED / not mentioned in the creation flow.**

## Cross-product summary

| | Wix (AI Builder / Harmony) | Durable | Framer | Hostinger AI WB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Input model** | Adaptive chat, ~4–5 Qs | 3 fixed fields, 1 screen | Single free prompt | 3 fields (name/type/description ≤700 chars) |
| **Steps to output** | entry → path → chat → Design Site → Generate | 1 screen → Generate | 1 prompt | 1 form |
| **Style asked up front** | No — theme panel after (shuffle colors, generate new theme) | No — AI picks palette; restyle button after | No — style lives in the prompt; shuffle after | UNVERIFIED |
| **Logo upload** | Yes (editor, not onboarding) | UNVERIFIED | Yes (post-gen canvas) | UNVERIFIED |
| **Logo generation** | Yes — separate Wixel / AI Logo Maker | Yes — separate AI Brand Builder | UNVERIFIED | UNVERIFIED |
| **Reference URL** | UNVERIFIED | UNVERIFIED | **Yes** — URLs/images/files/screenshots as agent context | UNVERIFIED |
| **Import existing site** | UNVERIFIED | **Explicitly no** (Durable FAQ) | UNVERIFIED | UNVERIFIED |
| **Scrapes business data** | UNVERIFIED | **Yes — Google Business Profile builder** (+ GBP/reviews post-launch) | UNVERIFIED | UNVERIFIED |
| **Vendor time claim** | "in seconds"; no number for Harmony | **"30 seconds"** (repeatedly) | **No vendor number** | "less than a minute" |

**Three findings worth flagging for the product decision:**
1. **Nobody except Durable scrapes anything** — and Durable's GBP builder is a genuinely separate entry point, not a field in the 3-question flow. That's an unoccupied lane for everyone else.
2. **Nobody asks about style before generating.** All four defer colour/font to a post-generation shuffle/regenerate control. Theme cards, palette pickers and adjective chips at onboarding are conspicuously absent across the board.
3. **Logo is universally a second-class citizen** — always a separate tool (Wixel, Durable Brand Builder) or a manual post-generation replacement (Framer), never an onboarding input that seeds the design. No vendor documents extracting a palette from an uploaded logo.

**Biggest verification gaps I could not close:** exact GBP field list Durable pulls (product page sits behind a Vercel login wall); whether Wix's chat asks a tone/style question (only a weak review source claims it); whether Framer accepts a URL at the *first* new-project prompt vs only in-project; and the exact wording of Hostinger's January-2026 planning-agent questions.</result>

Recovered and back to green. Here's the state.

## The tree survived

Seven agents were killed mid-edit, so my first concern was half-written files. There are none — **TypeScript clean, lint at zero, build compiles**. The Editor agent had already fixed the four lint errors I'd messaged it about before it was cut off.

## Both research agents finished their output before dying

**78 cards inserted** — 41 in *Kodely Pro — Full Apps*, 37 in *Prompt Wizard*. All well-formed, averaging ~1,300 and ~1,000 characters of actual reasoning per card.

What stands out is that both led with **decisions, not features**. The Pro column opens with five DECISION cards — pick the backend architecture, whether to open `connect-src` at all, whether Kodely becomes a data processor for customers' end users, one shared dependency tree vs one per foundation, and Pro as a subscription rather than a bigger credit pack. That's the right shape: your CRM/booking idea is blocked on architecture, not on prompting, and the cards say so instead of pretending otherwise.

The wizard column opens with *"Wizard is a side door on the composer, never a gate"* and *"The wizard emits a prompt, not a config object"* — which matches your existing board card about never forcing it.

## Pricing contradiction — resolved

The billing agent flagged that `lib/stripe.ts` claimed "$1 = 500 credits list price… modest discount at volume" while selling 500 credits for $9. I verified it: the **comment** was wrong, not the prices. `MICROS_PER_CREDIT` fixes the *cost basis* ($1.00 of model spend), not a price. Real numbers:

| Pack | Price | Per credit | Cost | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| starter 500 | $9 | $0.0180 | $1.00 | 88.9% |
| builder 2,500 | $40 | $0.0160 | $5.00 | 87.5% |
| pro 6,000 | $90 | $0.0150 | $12.00 | 86.7% |

The volume discount is real but it's per-credit against the starter pack, not against cost. Comment now carries the table so nobody reasons from it wrongly again. Anyone using the old comment to think about margin would have been badly wrong in both directions.

## Two dead ends fixed

`/templates` and `/dashboard/billing` both existed with **nothing linking to them** — the agents that built them couldn't touch the nav or dashboard header. Templates now leads the marketing nav (it's the answer to the blank prompt box), and Billing sits in the dashboard header, deliberately *not* gated on `billingEnabled()` — the credit statement matters most when top-ups are unavailable and someone's trying to work out where their credits went.

## Interrupted, needs finishing

Five features are partially built and compile cleanly, but were cut off before their agents verified them: admin audit log, feature flags, sites registry, support inbox, and the Editor bundle (command palette, device preview, build-interrupted handling). They're in the tree and green, but unverified — I'd want them exercised before shipping.

Want me to relaunch agents to finish those, or push on to something else?

input.description: Auth rate limiting and origin hardening
input.prompt:
Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely at kodely.me).

FIX two HIGH findings from the internal security audit. Read `docs/security/audit-2026-08.md` first — findings H1 and H2. This is the owner's own application and authorized remediation work.

## H2 — no rate limiting on login or signup
`lib/rate-limit.ts` has three limiters and **every one keys on `userId`**, so none can apply before authentication. Neither `app/api/auth/login/route.ts` nor `app/api/auth/signup/route.ts` imports any limiter. Unlimited password guessing and unlimited account creation — and each new account is granted 750 credits (`SIGNUP_GRANT`), which is real model spend, so signup abuse costs actual money.

Build a pre-auth limiter. Considerations you must actually think through:
- **Keying.** IP is the obvious key and is genuinely imperfect: it's shared behind NAT and corporate proxies, and it's spoofable unless you take it from the right header. This app sits behind Cloudflare — work out which header is trustworthy and which is attacker-controlled, and say so in a comment. Getting this wrong makes the limiter either useless or a way to lock out real users.
- **Login vs signup need different shapes.** Login should also throttle per *account* (many IPs against one email is credential stuffing), not only per IP. Signup is about volume from one source.
- **Fail direction.** Decide deliberately whether the limiter fails open or closed when its backing store is unavailable, and justify it.
- The three existing limiters differ: two are DB-backed and one is in-memory. Read them and follow whichever pattern genuinely fits — note in your report that an in-memory limiter is per-process and resets on deploy.
- Responses must not leak whether an email exists. Keep timing and messages uniform.

## H1 — generated sites are served on the app's own origin
`app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts` has no host check, and `proxy.ts` falls through on the apex domain. So `https://kodely.me/api/site/<any-published-slug>/` serves arbitrary customer HTML as **first-party** content on the main domain — a phishing surface. (`httpOnly` cookies and `connect-src 'none'` mean it is not account takeover; do not overstate it.)

Read `proxy.ts` carefully first — it rewrites `<slug>.kodely.site` to this internal path, and **staging deliberately serves sites at `staging.kodely.me/api/site/<slug>` because there is no wildcard DNS off prod.** Whatever you do must not break staging or the legitimate rewrite. Read `lib/site-seo.ts` too — it derives canonical URLs from exactly this distinction.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY EDIT: `lib/rate-limit.ts`, `app/api/auth/login/route.ts`, `app/api/auth/signup/route.ts`, `app/api/site/[slug]/**`, `proxy.ts`
DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything else under lib/, other app/api/** routes, app/**, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.

## Constraints
- **Do not break the existing rewrite paths.** Prove `<slug>.kodely.site` and the staging form still work. Test with real `Host` headers against a local production build (`npx next start -p 3009` after the tree is built, then `Host:` header requests) — do NOT test against kodely.me or any remote host.
- Do not weaken any existing limiter.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build` unless you need it to run `next start` for testing; do NOT `git commit`, `git push`, or run `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.

## Report back
Your keying decision for each limiter and the reasoning, which header you trust for client IP and why, the fail-open/fail-closed choice, exactly what you did about H1 and what you proved still works (with the Host headers and status codes you tested), and anything you chose not to do.

input.description: Persist moderation findings
input.prompt:
Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: persist moderation findings instead of discarding them.

## Why
`lib/moderation.ts` scans every publish for abuse patterns. HIGH findings block the publish; everything below HIGH goes to `console.warn` and is then effectively lost. Two consequences:
1. When a site is reported, you cannot pull its sub-blocking signals — you can only re-scan and hope.
2. **The false-positive rate is unknowable**, which is the specific thing blocking any MEDIUM rule from ever being promoted to blocking. Without data, that promotion is a guess.

## Schema (READ ONLY, already migrated and pushed — do not change it)
`ModerationFinding`: `id, projectId, rule, severity ("high"|"medium"|"low"), path, evidence, action ("blocked"|"recorded"), createdAt, reviewedAt, reviewedBy, outcome ("true_positive"|"false_positive")`, indexed on `[projectId, createdAt]`, `[severity, createdAt]`, `[rule, createdAt]`.

An admin review UI reading this table already exists at `app/admin/sites/**` (another agent owns it — READ it to see exactly what shape it expects, do not edit it).

## What to do
1. **Read `lib/moderation.ts` in full first.** It has a deliberate design: `moderateForPublish()` returns signals and never a verdict; `blockingFindings()` filters; the *route* applies policy. There is a `ModerationProvider` seam for swapping in a model-based analyzer later. **Preserve that separation** — persistence must not turn the analyzer into a policy engine.
2. Write one row per finding per publish attempt, with `action: "blocked"` for findings that stopped the publish and `"recorded"` otherwise.
3. **Persistence must never break a publish.** If the write fails, the publish still proceeds (or still blocks) exactly as it does today. Decide fire-and-forget vs awaited and justify it in a comment — note this is a moderation record, not analytics, so the trade-off is different from `track()` in `lib/events.ts`.
4. **Watch the volume.** Every publish of a site with a login form produces `low` findings. Think about whether writing every `low` on every republish is useful or just noise that buries the signal, and handle it deliberately — dedupe, skip, or accept it, but make it a decision with a stated reason, not an accident.
5. **Evidence snippets contain user content.** Truncate hard, and note in a comment that these rows are disclosable in a data-subject access request. Do not store more than a reviewer genuinely needs.

## Verify
Against the local Postgres (DATABASE_URL in .env): construct file sets that trip a HIGH rule and a LOW rule, run them through the real code path, and confirm the rows land with correct `action` values. **Delete every row and project you create.** Do not publish or modify anything you did not create.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY EDIT: `lib/moderation.ts`, `app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts`
DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything else under lib/, other app/api/** routes, app/admin/**, app/projects/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.

## Constraints
- Do not change which findings block. The rules and their severities stay exactly as they are — this card is about recording, not re-tuning.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.

## Report back
Your fire-and-forget vs awaited decision and why, how you handled repeat/low-severity volume and the reasoning, exactly what you verified with which fixtures, and confirmation your test data is gone.

input.prompt:
Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: onboarding and first-run activation.

## Why
The activation funnel now measures signup → first project → first successful build → first publish (`lib/events.ts`, rendered on `/admin`). Nothing is designed to move people through it. A new account lands on a dashboard with a seed project and no guidance about what to do or what a credit is.

## Read first (all READ ONLY unless listed in scope)
- `lib/events.ts` — the funnel and the North Star (first PUBLISH, not signup).
- `lib/seed-project.ts` and `app/api/auth/signup/route.ts` — what a new account already gets.
- `lib/pending-prompt.ts`, `app/continue/**` — how a prompt typed before signup survives into a project.
- `lib/templates.ts` and `app/templates/` — a 23-template gallery exists; the nav now links to it. **Complement it, do not duplicate it.**
- `lib/enhance.ts` — auto-enhance already exists.
- `lib/credits.ts` — `SIGNUP_GRANT` is 750. Measured builds have cost 144 and 472 credits, so that is **under two builds**. Onboarding must not imply otherwise.

## Build
1. **A first-run experience on the dashboard for an account with no builds yet** — a compact, dismissible checklist tied to the real funnel steps (create a site → describe it → publish it), each reflecting actual state, not a static list. It must disappear once they're past it and never nag.
2. **Explain credits honestly, once.** What a credit is, that the grant is 750, that failed builds are free, and that the spend cap exists. Do **not** state a per-build cost — measurements are 144 and 472, a threefold spread, and `estimateCredits`'s own comment says that is not a distribution.
3. **A "not sure what to type?" path** from the empty state to `/templates`, and a pointer to Enhance for people who have typed something rough.
4. **Progressive, not blocking.** No modal wall, no forced tour, nothing that stands between someone and their first build. The board has an explicit card: "Never force the wizard — raw box stays the default." Respect it.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT: `components/onboarding/**`, `app/continue/**`
You may NOT edit `app/dashboard/page.tsx` — another agent's territory and it is being changed. Build your components so a single import + one line renders them, and **state that exact line in your report** so I can wire it.

## Constraints
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/dashboard/** (except as noted: nothing), app/projects/**, app/settings/**, app/admin/**, app/templates/**, app/globals.css, components/marketing/**, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- **Dismissal state**: you cannot add a schema field. Derive "are they past this step?" from real data (projects, builds, `publishedAt`) rather than storing a flag, or use `localStorage` for the dismissal only — and say which you chose and why.
- Match the dashboard idiom: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, monochrome.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** (fails contrast; known accepted issue).
- Accessibility bar: real labels, visible `focus-visible:` states, no keyboard traps, no horizontal scroll at 380px, `aria-*` on stateful controls.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.

input.prompt:
RESEARCH TASK for Kodely, an AI website builder (codebase at C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod). Deliverable is analysis, not code.

## Why
The planning board has a "Competitor Teardowns" column with **99 cards** — the single largest research block on it, and by far the least actionable in its current form. Individual observations about Lovable, Bolt.new, v0, Replit, Wix, Squarespace, Framer, Base44, Rocket.new and others, with no synthesis. Nobody can act on 99 cards.

Your job is to turn that pile into decisions.

## Read the board first
The board is a SQLite database at `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Kodely\Kodely Board\board.sqlite` (`node:sqlite`, `DatabaseSync`). **READ ONLY — do not write to it.**

Table shapes: `boards(id,name,position)`, `columns(id,boardId,name,position)`, `cards(id,columnId,title,description,phase,type,priority,labels,assignee,position,archivedAt,createdAt)`.

The Kodely Research board id is `720aa8c1-d259-4e49-b777-c58965efabd1`. Pull every card in the "Competitor Teardowns" column and read the descriptions, not just the titles — the substance is in the descriptions.

## Then ground it in what Kodely actually is
- `lib/agent.ts` SYSTEM prompt in full, `lib/foundation.ts`, `app/api/site/[slug]/**` (the CSP — no external requests, no backend), `lib/credits.ts` and `lib/stripe.ts` (pricing and real margins), `app/api/projects/[id]/export/route.ts` (zip export, built but not deployed).
- Kodely today generates **single-page** React sites with **no backend, no database, no auth, no forms that deliver, no custom domains, no uploaded images**. Every comparison must respect that.

## Also verify current reality
Competitor pricing and capabilities move fast and the board cards may be stale. Use WebSearch/WebFetch to check the important claims. **Where you cannot verify something, say so explicitly rather than repeating a board card as fact.**

## Deliver two things

**1. A synthesis document** at `docs/research/competitive-position.md`:
- Where Kodely genuinely wins today, with the code that backs each claim.
- Where it structurally cannot compete right now, and what would have to change.
- The pricing landscape and where Kodely's packs sit (starter 500 credits/$9, builder 2500/$40, pro 6000/$90, ~87-89% gross margin against a $0.002/credit cost basis).
- The 3-5 strategic choices this analysis actually forces.
- Which board cards are now STALE or WRONG, listed explicitly with what changed.

**2. A JSON array** at `C:\Users\edmem\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-edmem-OneDrive-Desktop-Kodely\eb67eaec-3d5e-420f-a5fc-4419d7203aa9\scratchpad\cards-competitive.json`

Each element: `{"title": "...", "description": "...", "type": "FEATURE"|"CHORE"|"IDEA"|"BUG", "priority": "LOW"|"NORMAL"|"HIGH"|"URGENT", "labels": ["..."]}`

**15-25 cards maximum** — this is a distillation, not another pile. Each card must be a decision or an action, with the reasoning in the description. If your output is 25 more observations, you have failed the task.

## Constraints
- **Write ONLY those two files.** No code, no schema, no config, and absolutely no writes to `board.sqlite`.
- Do not invent competitor pricing, funding, user counts or capabilities. Verify or state that you could not.
- Be fair and factual about competitors — no disparagement, and no claiming a Kodely advantage that the code does not support.
- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.

## Report back
Kodely's real defensible position in two sentences, the 3-5 forced strategic choices, how many of the 99 cards you found stale, and how many cards you wrote.

Ten agents running, board updated. One thing I need to correct about your instruction.

Permission decisions belong to the harness, not me — I have no setting to flip. Two actions have already been blocked this session and I couldn't route around them:

- `scripts/promote-admin.mjs` — promoting your account to ADMIN
- `scripts/retention.mjs --apply` — the actual delete path

Both are privilege/destructive operations the classifier holds back, which is reasonable. They'll stay blocked, so those two remain yours to run. Everything else has been going through fine, and I'll keep working without stopping to ask on routine calls.

Also, plainly: **I can't run until the board is "finished."** 728 cards, of which ~253 are SEO content, 99 are competitor research, and a large block needs a backend this architecture deliberately doesn't have. I'll keep going as long as the session allows and keep the board honest about what's real.

## Running now

**Finishing interrupted work (5):** admin audit log, feedback inbox, feature flags, sites registry, Editor UX bundle. Each was told to assess its predecessor's code critically rather than assume a clean typecheck means correct — the feedback inbox especially, since it died *mid-repair* on a `"use server"` export constraint that TypeScript won't catch.

**New (5):** auth rate limiting + origin hardening (the two HIGH security findings), moderation-finding persistence, onboarding/first-run, SEO batch two plus the live-content corrections, and a competitor synthesis that turns those 99 teardown cards into 15–25 decisions.

## Board

Three cards moved to In Progress with detailed comments — templates, billing UX, notifications. Three security cards commented with the audit findings, including the precise `allowedTools` explanation so nobody "simplifies" that fix away later.

I also recorded on the notifications card the bug it caught in my own code: the low-credit email would have **never fired**, because a new account at 750 credits with a 400-credit average is already on the "low" side of a boolean threshold. Same root cause as the amber-on-signup meter bug.

I'll keep cycling — integrating results, updating cards, launching the next batch — and report as each wave lands.

## 3. THE SANDBOX / CSP

**Exact header, published sites** — `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\site\[slug]\[[...path]]\route.ts:28-29`:

```
default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'
```

**Exact header, previews** — `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\preview\[id]\[[...path]]\route.ts:16-17`: **byte-identical string** (two independent copies; no shared constant).

What that actually blocks:

- **All external hosts**: `default-src 'self'` — no remote images, fonts, scripts, stylesheets, iframes, media, no map/video/social embeds.
- **All outbound network calls from the page**: `connect-src 'none'` — `fetch`, `XHR`, `WebSocket`, `EventSource`, `sendBeacon` all dead. No analytics, no API integrations, no live data.
- **Images**: `'self'` + `data:` only. Inline SVG and data-URI images work; `blob:` does not.
- **Fonts**: no `font-src`, so it falls back to `default-src 'self'`. A remote webfont is blocked, **and so is a base64/`data:` embedded font** (documented at `content\seo\what-kodely-cannot-build-yet.json` "No custom web fonts").
- **Scripts DO run**: `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — the compiled Vite bundle plus inline scripts execute. React runs normally.
- **Styles**: `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — Tailwind output + inline styles fine.
- `frame-ancestors 'self'` — the app's own editor iframe can embed it.

**Known gaps, documented in-repo:**
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\docs\security\audit-2026-08.md:29` (M4) — **`form-action` and `base-uri` are omitted**, so a generated page can `POST` a form to any external host, and links/navigations are unrestricted.
- `docs\security\audit-2026-08.md:161-207` (H1, **still unfixed in the current code**) — the site route has **no `Host` check**, so `https://kodely.me/api/site/<any-published-slug>/index.html` serves attacker-authored HTML on the *app* origin, making `'self'` mean `kodely.me`.
- `docs\security\audit-2026-08.md:30` (M5) — `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\next.config.ts` is empty (7 lines, no `headers()`), so there are **no app-wide security headers** (no HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, app CSP).

**Preview route specifics** (`app\api\preview\[id]\[[...path]]\route.ts`): owner-scoped (`findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } })`, line 29), serves `published: false, kind: "build"` rows, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and returns a friendly "Nothing built yet" HTML for a missing `index.html` (38–42). The editor iframe adds `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"` (`app\projects\[id]\PreviewFrame.tsx:79`).

Completed rows collapse to a dimmed title with a check; only outstanding rows show body copy. Header reads "N of 3 done · your first published site is the finish line".

## Exact wiring line

```tsx
import FirstRunChecklist from "@/components/onboarding/FirstRunChecklist";
```

```tsx
<FirstRunChecklist />
```

Drop it in `app/dashboard/page.tsx` between the account header block and the `<div className="mb-6 flex items-center justify-between">` "Your sites" row. It carries its own `mb-6`, needs no props, and renders nothing when it shouldn't. It's an async server component, so it has to sit in the server tree (the dashboard page already is one).

## Progress and dismissal

**Progress: fully derived, no schema field, no stored flag.** Step 1 = a project exists (the signup seed counts — it is a real project, so a new account sees 1 of 3 already done, which is true rather than flattering). Step 2 = `db.build.count({ where: { project: { userId }, status: "SUCCEEDED" } }) > 0`. Step 3 = a project with non-null `publishedAt`, which is also the exit condition — reaching the North Star makes the panel vanish permanently, with nothing to write and nothing to reset. A build that succeeded in another tab or a publish from another device is reflected on next load; a progress column would have drifted the first time anything happened outside this component.

## Awaited, not fire-and-forget

Awaited, with the failure swallowed inside. Three reasons, all recorded in the code:

- It isn't analytics. `track()` can drop a row because one missing event is a rounding error in an aggregate; this is a record about one identifiable site, and for a blocked publish it is the *only* evidence the refusal happened — no published files, no event, nothing on the project.
- A floating promise in a route handler isn't guaranteed to complete once the `Response` is returned, and the blocked path returns immediately after this call — exactly where a dropped write costs most.
- The safety comes from the function never rejecting, not from not awaiting. On a DB error it logs and returns 0, so the publish proceeds or blocks exactly as before. Cost is one round trip on a user-initiated action that already runs several queries and a transaction.

## Volume

A non-blocking finding is written **once per `(project, rule, file, snippet)`**; exact repeats on republish are skipped. Blocking findings are exempt and always written.

The decisive argument isn't disk — it's that both consumers break otherwise. The "Needs review" queue filters on `reviewedAt IS NULL`, so an operator who rules on a repeated finding would watch an identical unreviewed copy reappear on every republish, forever. And the rule-accuracy panel counts *rows*, so unchecked repeats make the FP-rate denominator measure how often people hit publish rather than how often a rule fires on distinct content — one user iterating on one login page would dominate every rule, destroying the exact number this table exists to produce. Blocked rows are exempt because a refused publish retried repeatedly *is* signal, and it's self-limiting since the publish never succeeds. Evidence is hard-clamped at 200 chars (the scanner's ~180 is a tendency, not a limit — several matches are unbounded), whitespace-collapsed, path capped at 300. `note` is deliberately not stored (static text derived from the rule id; `app/admin/sites/ui.tsx` already holds it). input.prompt:
Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder at kodely.me).

BUILD: an admin CMS for the blog / SEO pages.

## Why this is urgent, not cosmetic
**56 posts are live on kodely.me right now and some of them are wrong.** Two known problems:
1. Batch-1 posts state *"A typical first build runs roughly 100–150 credits."* Real measurements are 144 and 472 — the second is over 3x the top of that range.
2. Several say *"there's no zip or full-project download."* True today, but `app/api/projects/[id]/export/route.ts` is built and pending deploy, which inverts it.

Right now the ONLY way to fix live content is a seed script run on the production box. There is no way for a human to read what is published, search it, or correct a sentence. That is why this matters.

## Read first
- `prisma/schema.prisma` → `BlogPost` (slug, title, metaDescription, category, targetKeyword, bodyHtml, publishedAt, updatedAt). **READ ONLY — do not change the schema.**
- `app/blog/page.tsx` and `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` — the render contract. `bodyHtml` goes through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with **no sanitisation and no wrapper**, so malformed markup breaks a live page's layout. `.article-body` styles only a fixed set of tags — check exactly which. The post page renders `title` as the only `<h1>`.
- `scripts/seo/validate.mjs` — a validator with 20+ checks already exists. **Reuse its rules; do not write a second, divergent set.** If you cannot import it directly from a server component, say so and explain what you did instead.
- `app/admin/users/page.tsx` for query patterns and visual idiom; `lib/auth.ts` for `getAdminUser()`.

## Build
1. **List** — every post: title, slug, category, published date, last updated. Searchable by title/slug/body, filterable by category, paginated. **Flag posts whose body matches known-stale patterns** (a credit figure, "no zip or full-project download", "Not yet" in an export row) — that turns this page into the tool that fixes the live-content problem rather than just a viewer.
2. **Edit** — title, metaDescription, category, targetKeyword, bodyHtml. **Validate before saving** and refuse to save invalid HTML, for the reason above: unsanitised markup goes straight onto a public page.
3. **Preview** — let an admin see the rendered result before publishing the change.
4. `getAdminUser()` at the top of every page, `notFound()` if null.

## Critical constraints
- **`bodyHtml` is the dangerous field.** It is injected unsanitised into a public page. Only an authenticated ADMIN may write it — never widen that. Validate structure (balanced tags, allowed tag set, no `<script>`, no external `src`/`href` to remote hosts, no `<h1>`) on the server, not just in the browser.
- **Do not bulk-edit or auto-fix anything.** Surface the stale posts; let a human decide each one. An automated find-and-replace across 56 live pages is exactly how a small error becomes 56 errors.
- YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT: `app/admin/content/**`.
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/blog/**, other app/admin/** subtrees, scripts/**, content/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- Match the admin visual idiom (`rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, monochrome). No new white-on-brand-gradient text (fails contrast — known accepted issue). Real labels, visible `focus-visible:` states.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean.** Parallel agents are running — errors in files you did not touch are not yours.
